narrative.overview: One cool monochrome field, slate fading to black, kept open beside the editor all day. White (ink in light mode) is the only control colour of the default Black & White theme and the selection and focus colour of every theme; hue appears only when it means something, and the few numbers that matter speak in a tall condensed face. The views and behaviour of the app stay exactly as they are; only the visual layer changes. Inside this world the branch map reads as a line diagram: one hairline trunk carries the shipped releases as stations, branches hang off it as small boxes (a header and one info row), ahead/behind rides on the incoming line as a small chip, and their commits float free beneath them. One piece of the old look stays by owner decision: the flowing rainbow on anything an agent is working on. The palette ships as the Gitnetix Black & White pair (gitnetix-bw, gitnetix-bw-light), the default and what System follows; Gitnetix Dark/Light and the 34 third-party themes keep their palettes and take the same shapes, type, hairlines and map structure.
keyCharacteristics: Branch map as a station line: hairline trunk, ring stations, two-row boxes, ahead/behind chips on the lines, floating commits
White controls in Black & White (each other theme keeps its accent for controls); ink selection and focus everywhere
Hue reserved for add, delete, warn, conflict, and the rainbow on agent work
Antonio condensed for versions and headline numerals
2 to 3px corners, no pills, no glows outside agent work

rules.name: The Control Rule
rules.body: Ink (--fg) means this is yours: selection, active tab, segment and tag, check fills and focus, in every theme. --accent means you can press this and marks controls only: primary buttons, links, a few control states. In Black & White the accent is white (ink in light); other themes keep their own accent as their control colour. Never spend an accent on selection, focus, roles or status.

rules.name: The Meaning Rule
rules.body: Branch type, trunk, release and props carry no hue; a hue must mean added, deleted, warning or conflict. The one exception is the Agent Working rainbow.

rules.name: The Agent Working Rule
rules.body: Anything an agent is working on flows with the incumbent rainbow (g1 to g4 gradient text, colour-cycling icons and dot, soft g2 drop-shadow), and nothing else may. A waiting agent is Warn. Reduced motion stops it.

rules.name: The Theme Rule
rules.body: Black & White is the default and what System follows; every other theme (Gitnetix Dark/Light in app.css, the 34 third-party themes through tokens()) keeps its own ground, panel, text and accent, gets the derived steps (--line2, --link, --ground, --route, --g1 to --g4) mixed from its colours unless it sets them, and takes the same shapes, type, hairlines and map structure. Role hues are neutral in every theme: no component reads --trunk-fg, --release-fg, --prop-fg or --mod-fg for a role (tokens() still emits them for the marketing website, syntax highlighting and the agent-working rainbow read them).

rules.name: The One Loud Voice Rule
rules.body: Antonio only for screen and page titles, the welcome heading, the next release and headline numerals; shipped versions read in Mono.

rules.name: Flat at Rest
rules.body: No shadow on resting surfaces; only floating layers get the single float shadow.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every map line is a hairline: the route to the checked-out branch 1.5px in the route colour, other links 1px Link Dim, falling-behind links dashed 3/4. No thick transit lines, no hue on the route, no pulse, no glow.

dos: Do use ink for selection and focus in every theme, and --accent only for controls (white in Black & White)
Do show a disabled primary as the outline with a faint label
Do keep every view and behaviour where it is
Do show branch type as a text label
Do keep all themes working through the token layer
Do draw the branch map in hairlines: 1.5px route, 1px other links, dashed 3/4 when falling behind, 1px faint trunk
Do keep branch boxes to a header row and one info row, and let commits float beneath them with no container
Do put ahead/behind on the incoming line as a chip, a rebase button when there is a behind count
Do put shipped releases on the trunk as ring stations at an even 36px pitch, main as the large station where the route starts
Do mark everything an agent is working on with the flowing rainbow (the Agent Working Rule), and stop it under reduced motion
Do dock the agents panel right at 460px in both views
donts: Don't use gradient text, glows or drop-shadow filters, except the rainbow on agent work under the Agent Working Rule
Don't use the working hues for anything but an agent working; a waiting agent is Warn
Don't use pills or radii above 3px on rectangles
Don't give roles or branch types their own hue
Don't use spring or bounce easing
Don't draw thick transit lines or a coloured route on the branch map; the red route of the trunk reference is not adopted
Don't put commits inside a branch box or wrap them in a card on the map
Don't put ahead/behind inside the box, or a separate rebase button under the commits
